answer: Like a tide that admits one boat at a time through a narrow channel, the network gives each agent a chain of dependent tasks: the output of step one becomes the input of step two, up the terrace of stages. No step can start before its predecessor finishes, so work cannot be split across clones. An operator running fifty fake identities must climb fifty terraces in series, paying fifty times the time, while an honest agent climbs one. There is no oasis of cheap parallelism: every identity must spend real time, so Sybil scale costs the resource an attacker cannot fake - sequential attention.
